summary: Feed s167_triple to NDR is degraded with 3 high-severity faults: 97.8% encrypted traffic exceeds 90% tolerance, required VLAN 20 missing (50% untagged), and 68% GRE tunnel encapsulation obscuring inner traffic.

findings.root_cause: Traffic is forwarded to NDR without prior TLS decryption/inspection - 97.8% of bytes are encrypted vs 90% tolerance. Packet broker is not decrypting or not feeding decrypted copy from SSL visibility appliance.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires full payload for deep packet inspection and behavioral detection; with 98% encrypted it is blind to payloads, cannot detect C2, exfiltration, or lateral movement inside TLS.

recommended_fix.why: NDR needs_full_payload=true but cannot analyze encrypted bytes; decrypting (or mirroring decrypted copy) before the NDR restores visibility while respecting privacy policy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or TAP aggregation is stripping 802.1Q tags or trunk not forwarding VLAN 20 - 50% of packets arrive untagged and VLAN 20 never seen despite being required.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR loses tenant/segment context for VLANs 10,20; detection policies, asset grouping and VLAN-based anomaly detection fail, creating coverage gap for VLAN 20 traffic.

recommended_fix.why: Tool profile requires VLANs 10,20 for correct classification; preserving/restoring 802.1Q tags on the broker egress ensures NDR sees correct segmentation.

findings.root_cause: 68% of frames (1184/1742) arrive encapsulated in GRE and are forwarded without decapsulation on the packet broker; NDR sees only outer tunnel headers.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR analyzes outer GRE headers instead of inner IP/flows, missing true source/destination, ports and payloads; correlation, IDS signatures and behavioral models fail on tunneled traffic.

recommended_fix.why: Stripping GRE at the packet broker exposes inner packets for full NDR inspection, restoring L3-L7 visibility without changing tunnel transport.
